name: Drawing Knowledge
description:
What can we learn about place and people from a detailed drawing?

This exhibition presents one of the largest private collections of architectural drawings of Rajasthan’s forts and palaces, from Jaisalmer and Amber to Mehrangarh and Hawa Mahal. Each drawing is the product of years of research and meticulous documentation, recording the walls, courtyards, and water systems that shaped life inside these buildings.

Comprehensive documentation of such places is increasingly scarce. Made possible by the mentorship of Kulbhushan Jain and Minakshi Jain, the collection brings this accumulated knowledge into the public domain. It gives researchers, students, and curious visitors access to study the details closely, now and for generations to come.

**Exhibition Opening:** 6:30pm, Fri, Nov 13

**Exhibition Timings:** 11am – 8pm | Fri, Nov 13 – Sun, Nov 15

**Exhibition on show until:** 8pm | Sun, Nov 15

**Walkthroughs:**

6:30pm | Fri, Nov 13

11am & 5:30pm | Sat, Nov 14

11am & 5:30pm | Sun, Nov 15

**Beyond the Lines | 7pm – 8:30pm | Fri, Nov 13**

A panel discussion exploring how architectural drawings of Rajasthan’s forts and palaces serve as archives of architectural, social and cultural knowledge, and their potential for future scholarship.

**Built Before the Blueprint Workshop | 11:30am – 1:30pm | Sat, Nov 14\***

A collaborative workshop inviting participants to read architectural drawings from the exhibition to discover how Rajasthan’s forts and palaces responded to their climate, resources, water needs and military strategies.

**Health, Heritage and Architecture Workshop | 6pm – 8pm | Nov 14\***

A workshop exploring how traditional architecture created cool, airy, bright and healthy spaces without electricity, using drawings from the exhibition.

*\*To register for the Workshop, request you to write to support@bangaloreinternationalcentre.org with the workshop title and number of participants attending.*

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: The Quantum Life of Pi—How Chasing Strings Led to a New Formula for an Ancient Number
description:
**About the event**

Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

**About the lecture**

Six hundred years ago, Madhava of Sangamagrama, from Kerala, found a way to express Pi as an endless sum, centuries before Newton and Leibniz. One might imagine that after all these centuries, there would be very little left to discover about this familiar number.

As it turns out, quite a lot.

In 2024, while studying how strings scatter off one another, theoretical physicist Dr. Aninda Sinha and his postdoctoral researcher Arnab Priya Saha stumbled upon an entirely new infinite family of formulas for Pi.

The discovery emerged from an unlikely place. The researchers were investigating string theory, one of our most ambitious attempts at understanding the fundamental laws of the universe. They weren’t looking for Pi at all. It simply emerged from the equations describing how tiny strings collide.

Some of these new formulas even converge to Pi faster than Madhava’s celebrated series.

In this lecture, Dr. Sinha will take us through the mathematics, the history and the unexpected connections that led to this discovery. Along the way, he will make a larger argument about the importance of pursuing knowledge for its own sake.

Time and again, ideas pursued out of sheer curiosity, with no immediate practical application in sight, have gone on to shape technologies and transform our understanding of the world.

Expect a few stories, a little history and a fresh appreciation for the quiet usefulness of seemingly useless knowledge.

No mathematics degree required. Just curiosity (and, this being Pint of View, a drink in hand).

**About the Speaker**

Dr. Aninda Sinha is a theoretical physicist and Professor at the Centre for High Energy Physics, Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore. He is also a QHA Senior Fellow at the University of Calgary.

His research spans string theory, quantum field theory and the bootstrap, a fascinating approach to understanding the laws of physics using principles of consistency and symmetry.

In 2024, his work with postdoctoral researcher Arnab Priya Saha led to the discovery of a new infinite family of formulas for Pi, making headlines around the world.

Dr. Sinha is the recipient of several prestigious honours, including the ICTP Prize, the Wolfram Innovator Award and the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award (2019).

He is also a firm believer in the usefulness of useless knowledge, and in the idea that some of the most surprising discoveries begin with nothing more than curiosity.

**About Pint of View**

Pint of View is India's Largest Lecture Community. We brought the lecture in bar format to India and are now expanding across the globe with chapters in 15 cities worldwide. Here, big ideas meet intimate spaces, and you walk in curious and walk out with a sharper lens on the world.

Book now and develop your own pint of view. 🍻

name: Make your own Sashiko Bookmarks
description:
Japanese crafts are designed to be mindful, calming and skill-building, matching perfectly with our ethos at Knot Therapy.

Sashiko is an embroidery technique developed to preserve both garments and resources. Its unique style of using the minimum material by creating geometric patterns while reinforcing the fabric in such a way that it not only survives heavy use but the mending is decorative - the flaw becomes part of its beauty.

Join us to explore a brand new thread craft, some interesting history, make your very own bookmarks, all while learning a new technique to regulate yourself and make some calm with your own hands.

**What you get:**

4 sets of bookmarks to experiment with

Safe supplies to create the punch base

All tools & threads to create the embroidery

A guided and quiet experience, curated by your own pace & aesthetic.

**Open to Ages 16+**

name: Side A/Side B: Californication with Sachin Bhatt
description:
A listening session of **Californication, t**he album that gave the Chili Peppers a second life.

The **Red Hot Chili Peppers**' seventh record came out of the band's lowest years and turned into their biggest success. Frusciante came back to the band. The rap-rock novelty label fell away, and what replaced it was Kiedis writing his most reflective lyrics, Flea holding everything up from underneath, and some of the most thoughtful guitar playing at the turn of the century.

The session is hosted by **Sachin Bhatt,** a Bangalore artist who has spent years making visuals for some of music's most loved artists. He's an art director and a vinyl collector, and he makes music in his spare time. On Sunday he brings this record and the story behind his pick.
